[[File:June 2007 Chapultepec 3.jpg|thumb|Chapultepec]]
'''Chapultepec''' (''Grasshopper Hill'' in Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs) is [[Mexico City|Mexico City's]] principal park, "the green lung of the city". This hill has been important throughout the city's history as the perch of fortresses and palaces, and the manicured forest surrounding it now holds many of Mexico's greatest cultural treasures. The neighborhoods on either side are among the most affluent in the city.

==Understand==
This district centers on '''Chapultepec Park''' (''Bosque de Chapultepec''). It is Mexico City's largest park at {{hectare|866}} and includes wooded natural areas, winding pedestrian walkways and busy lakes. It also includes some of the city's top museums - the Museum of Anthropology is reason enough to visit Mexico City, and Chapultepec Castle (''Castillo de Chapultepec'') also makes its way into lots of itineraries.

The park is very large, with too many attractions to experience in a single day. You may want to focus on only one of the park's four sections, or limit yourself to only a few attractions.

The city publishes a [https://mexicocity.cdmx.gob.mx/locations/chapultepec-park/?lang=en Chapultepec Park Visitor Guide] which contains in-depth information on the park's features.

Northwest of the park is a wealthy residential neighborhood, Lomas de Chapultepec. Further out in the surrounding hills are more wealthy copycat neighborhoods collectively known as Las Lomas.

===History===
Chapultepec has been a landmark since the pre-Columbian era, when it became a retreat for Aztec rulers. In the colonial period, Chapultepec Castle was built atop the hill. It alternated between residential and military uses (it was the site of a Mexican-American War battle in 1847) until eventually becoming the official residence of Mexico's heads of state. It would remain so until 1934, when Los Pinos, in another area of the forest, became the presidential residence.

===On foot===

===By cable car===
'''Los Pinos Constituyentes''' Cablebus station (line 3) from [[Mexico City/Santa Fe|Santa Fe]] is close to Section 1 of the park. It provides access to a number of popular tourist spots including Los Pinos, Parque Aztlán, the Papalote Children's Museum, and the Museum of Natural History.

===By bus===
Long-distance buses from cities and states outside the Mexico City metropolitan area arrive and depart from '''Terminal de Autobuses Poniente''' (Observatorio), which is on the south side of Chapultepec, 1 km south of Av Constituyentes on Sur 122. Use Metro line 1 to station '''Observatorio'''.

==Get around==
===On foot===
It's a park so the obvious way to get around is to walk. This is the best option if you plan to just visit the biggest attractions of Section I (which is also the smallest section), or if you plan to just visit the museums of Section II (which cluster close to the park edge along Av Constituyentes).
 
===By bike===
Chapultepec is a big park... ''really'' big. If you plan to explore the northern parts of Section II or much of Section III or Section IV, your best option is to rent a bike and get around by pedal power. Most roads, walkways, and trails are paved so the ride is smooth though there are a lot of hills once you get into Section III and Section IV.
* {{go
| name=Casa de la Bici Bosque | alt= | url= | email=

| wikidata=
| lastedit=
| content=Friendly bike rental kiosk that has been a fixture of the park since 1921. Many bikes to choose from including sizes for children. Check bike condition before leaving because you don't want to break down and have to walk the bike a long way back. Drinks and snacks for sale. Restroom available for M$5.
}}

The city's '''[https://ecobici.cdmx.gob.mx/ Ecobici]''' program has several rental kiosks on the major avenues that border the park and there are kiosks in Section I and Section II that may be better options. Ecobici does not have children's bikes. (''See also [[Cycling in Mexico City]]''.)

Chapultepec Park is organized into four major sections, from northeast to southwest:

===Section I===
[[File:Chapultepec Castle interior.jpg|thumb|Castillo de Chapultepec (''Chapultepec Castle'')]]
This is the most tourist-friendly section and is the best section for a first-time visitor with limited time to explore the city. It is the area closest to Paseo de la Reforma and is close to many of the city's biggest high-rise hotels.

| hours=Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00 | price=Adult M$210, Mexican citizens and residents M$105 (ID required); seniors over 60, children under 13, teachers: free; free on Sundays for Mexican citizens and residents; video camera and flash photography is not permitted

| wikidata=Q1072510
| content=The imposing castle on top of the hill calls to visitors. Over its history, it has been the home of the Spanish Viceroys, a military college, a scene of historic battle during the Mexican-American War, the palace of Emperor Maximilian and Empress Carlotta, the national observatory, and the presidential palace. It is now a museum. You can walk about 1 km up the winding hill road, or take the tram that departs every twenty minutes for M$13. There are two parts to the museum: the '''Alcazar''' (with the exhibits on the life of its former residents – the emperor and the presidents), and the '''Castillo''' (now the Museum of National History). Both are decorated with remarkable murals depicting the nation's and the site's history. Don't miss the Roman-style gardens and observatory on the roof of the Alcazar. The castle also boasts a fine view of Mexico City and its surroundings. While visiting the site, you can leave your bag in the locker room for a fee near the entry to the site (at the bottom of the hill). Storing your bag is mandatory if it contains any food, and you will need to empty your water bottle at the top.
}}

===Section II===
This is a more natural area with fewer strolling tourists, but it includes some very significant sites that will be of interest to certain kinds of tourists and some museums that are ideally suited to families traveling to [[Mexico City with children]]. Most of the museums are in the south end of the section and are most easily reached via Metro to the Constituyentes station.

===Section III===
This is a natural area that is used by active fitness fans for running, hiking and biking as well as the odd urban naturalist who needs to escape traffic and the built-up world to hug a few trees. There are no major tourist attractions in this section (which is just the way people who enjoy the outdoors like it). 

===Section IV===
The newest section of Chapultepec used to be known as ''Industrias Militares'' and was owned by Mexico's Department of Defense (SEDENA) where they operated military maintenance shops and similar facilities. It includes rugged terrain with hills, cliffs, and rough rocky backcountry.

If you are on the northern side of Chapultepec (near the Museum of Anthropology or the Rufino Tamayo Museum, you may find some excellent nearby restaurants in the [[Mexico City/Polanco#Eat|Polanco neighborhood]]. If you are on the south side of the park, the restaurants of nearby [[Mexico City/Condesa and Roma#Eat|Condesa]] offer some great dining opportunities.

==Drink==
Soft drinks and bottled water are sold by sidewalk vendors throughout Section I of the park. Plan to bring your own drinks if you are visiting other, less heavily used sections of the park. Numerous restaurants in the park sell drinks (including alcoholic beverages) and nearby neighborhoods like Polanco and Condesa have numerous restaurants and convenience stores.

==Sleep==
Much of the area of this district is public park land so travelers will find many more hotels in neighboring districts that border Chapultepec. Parts of the nearby districts are within easy walking distance (no more than 2 Km) from Chapultepec Park. Look for more hotels in [[Mexico City/Polanco|Polanco]], [[Mexico City/Zona Rosa|Zona Rosa/Reforma]], and [[Mexico City/Condesa and Roma|Condesa]].

==Connect==
All of Mexico City has excellent 5G cellular coverage with virtually no dead zones. Broadband internet is ubiquitous and almost all hotels and restaurants offer WiFi service. The city government also provides free WiFi access in public spaces such as local parks. See parent article for [[Mexico City]] for more details.
